title: The Experiment That Looked Too Successful
title_ja: 成功しすぎて見えた実験
fact_notes: 生徒・家族・実験は架空の教育用事例。英文・和訳・問題・解説は独自に制作。

sentences.en: A science club tests whether different materials can keep a glass of water cool on a warm afternoon.
sentences.ja: 科学クラブは暖かい午後に異なる材料がコップの水を冷たく保てるか調べます。

sentences.en: Students place three identical glasses in a classroom and wrap two of them with different materials.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは同じコップ三つを教室に置き、二つを異なる材料で包みます。

sentences.en: Their first measurements suggest that one material works much better than the others.
sentences.ja: 最初の測定では一つの材料がほかよりずっと効果的に見えます。

sentences.en: However, a student notices that this glass was placed closer to the open window.
sentences.ja: しかしある生徒はそのコップが開いた窓の近くに置かれていたと気づきます。

sentences.en: The group begins to wonder whether the result came from the material or from its position.
sentences.ja: グループは結果が材料によるものか位置によるものか疑問を抱きます。

sentences.en: The teacher asks them to examine the conditions before announcing that the experiment proved anything.
sentences.ja: 教師は実験が何かを証明したと発表する前に条件を調べるよう求めます。

sentences.en: The students learn that an experiment can be difficult to interpret when several conditions change together.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは複数の条件が一緒に変わると実験の解釈が難しくなると学びます。

sentences.en: For example, sunlight, air movement, and the starting temperature of water may influence a final reading.
sentences.ja: 例えば日光、空気の動き、水の最初の温度は最終の数値に影響するかもしれません。

sentences.en: If these factors are not considered, a difference may be attributed to the wrong cause.
sentences.ja: これらの要因を考えなければ違いを誤った原因に結びつけるかもしれません。

sentences.en: The group checks whether its glasses contained equal amounts of water and were measured at similar times.
sentences.ja: グループはコップの水の量が等しく、同じような時刻に測られたか確認します。

sentences.en: They realize that the attractive result was not enough to establish why one glass stayed cooler.
sentences.ja: 魅力的な結果だけでは一つのコップが冷たく保たれた理由は確定できないと気づきます。

sentences.en: The class decides to keep both the original observations and a record of the possible weaknesses.
sentences.ja: クラスは最初の観察と考えられる弱点の記録を両方残すと決めます。

sentences.en: During a second trial, students place the glasses in comparable positions and check the water at regular intervals.
sentences.ja: 二度目の試験で生徒たちは同じような位置にコップを置き、一定の間隔で水を確認します。

sentences.en: Instead of changing the materials and the locations at once, they focus on comparing the coverings.
sentences.ja: 材料と場所を同時に変えるのでなく、覆いの違いに集中します。

sentences.en: They also make sure the same measuring method is used for every glass.
sentences.ja: すべてのコップに同じ測定方法を使うようにもします。

sentences.en: The new results show a smaller difference than the first experiment appeared to suggest.
sentences.ja: 新しい結果では最初の実験が示したように見えるほどの大きな差はありません。

sentences.en: Some students are disappointed because the earlier result seemed more exciting.
sentences.ja: 先の結果の方が興味深く見えたため残念に思う生徒もいます。

sentences.en: Their teacher explains that reducing an error is a scientific success even when the final result is less dramatic.
sentences.ja: 教師は最終結果が地味でも誤りを減らすことは科学的な成功だと説明します。

sentences.en: The club repeats the test on another day to see whether a similar pattern appears again.
sentences.ja: クラブは似た傾向が再び現れるか別の日に試験を繰り返します。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the students avoid claiming that a few classroom trials can answer every question about insulation.
sentences.ja: それでも教室での数回の試験ですべての断熱の問いに答えられるとは主張しません。

sentences.en: They discuss how the results might differ with another material, a different room, or a longer testing period.
sentences.ja: 別の材料、違う部屋、より長い試験期間なら結果がどう変わるか話し合います。

sentences.en: They report which observations were repeated and which conditions were still difficult to control.
sentences.ja: 繰り返し確認できた観察とまだ管理しにくかった条件を報告します。

sentences.en: The students also distinguish what their measurements show from explanations that remain uncertain.
sentences.ja: 測定値が示すことと不確かなままの説明も区別します。

sentences.en: A careful report can be useful even when it does not produce a simple answer.
sentences.ja: 簡単な答えが出なくても慎重な報告は役立つ場合があります。

sentences.en: At the club's final presentation, students show the original data, the revised results, and the reasons for testing again.
sentences.ja: クラブの最終発表で生徒たちは元のデータと修正後の結果と再試験の理由を示します。

sentences.en: They explain why the position of a glass might have influenced their first conclusion.
sentences.ja: コップの位置が最初の結論に影響した可能性を説明します。

sentences.en: As a result, the audience begins asking more questions about measurement methods instead of accepting a surprising number immediately.
sentences.ja: その結果聞き手は驚く数字をすぐ受け入れず測定方法についてさらに質問するようになります。

sentences.en: The group learns that uncertainty is not always a problem to hide but can guide better experiments.
sentences.ja: グループは不確かさが必ずしも隠すべき問題ではなくよりよい実験へ導くものにもなると学びます。

sentences.en: Scientific progress often depends on discovering what a first result fails to explain.
sentences.ja: 科学の進歩は最初の結果が説明できないことの発見に左右される場合が多いのです。

sentences.en: A trustworthy investigation values honest revision more than an impressive-looking conclusion.
sentences.ja: 信頼できる調査は印象的な結論より誠実な修正を大切にします。

questions.prompt: What difference does a student notice in the first experiment?
options: One glass is closer to an open window.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「しかしある生徒はそのコップが開いた窓の近くに置かれていたと気づきます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher delay a conclusion?
options: The school does not allow science projects.
The glasses are completely different sizes.
The students have not chosen a title.
The conditions may have affected the measurements.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「教師は実験が何かを証明したと発表する前に条件を調べるよう求めます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Which conditions might affect the result?
options: Sunlight, air movement, and starting temperature.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「例えば日光、空気の動き、水の最初の温度は最終の数値に影響するかもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the group recognize about its first result?
options: It shows every experiment will work the same way.
It cannot establish the cause of the difference alone.
It proves the material has no effect.
It makes a second trial unnecessary.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「魅力的な結果だけでは一つのコップが冷たく保たれた理由は確定できないと気づきます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is kept more consistent in the second trial?
options: The time spent writing the report.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「材料と場所を同時に変えるのでなく、覆いの違いに集中します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher call the revised experiment a success?
options: It produces the most dramatic difference.
It proves that all materials are equal.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「教師は最終結果が地味でも誤りを減らすことは科学的な成功だと説明します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does the club repeat the trial another day?
options: To produce a more exciting photograph.
To check whether the pattern appears again.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「それでも教室での数回の試験ですべての断熱の問いに答えられるとは主張しません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What do students distinguish in the report?
options: The school timetable and sports results.
The price and appearance of the glasses.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「測定値が示すことと不確かなままの説明も区別します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the audience respond to the final presentation?
options: By asking more about methods and conditions.
By deciding that all future tests are unnecessary.
By demanding only the highest number.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「グループは不確かさが必ずしも隠すべき問題ではなくよりよい実験へ導くものにもなると学びます。」が根拠です。

options: The most dramatic initial result is always the most accurate.
Uncertainty should be hidden from reports.
Repeating tests makes science less trustworthy.
A reliable experiment requires examining errors and revising conclusions.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「信頼できる調査は印象的な結論より誠実な修正を大切にします。」が根拠です。
